metaDescription: How to begin, and how Becky keeps you safe — what's needed beforehand, what should be settled first, and when this work isn't the right path.
heading: This isn't right for everyone — and that's said with care
intro: Some of what follows may read like a list of rules. It isn't. Every line exists to keep you safe, and Becky would far rather tell you honestly that this isn't your path than take you somewhere that could harm you.
crisisCalloutStrong: If you're in danger of hurting yourself right now
crisisCalloutBeforeNumber: , please don't wait for an appointment — call or text
crisisCalloutAfterNumber: to reach someone straight away, or 911 in an emergency. You deserve help sooner than a website can offer it.
requirementsIntro: Not hurdles — just the circle of support that makes this work safe and lasting.
requirements: Have a regular doctor who knows you, so someone is keeping an eye on your general health — particularly your heart and your breathing.
Have a therapist in your life — either someone you already see, or someone you begin seeing as this work starts.
Sit down for an unhurried conversation about your history, so you and Becky can decide together whether this is right for you.
treatFirstIntro: These don't close the door — they just need looking after before you begin. Often it's a matter of one conversation with your doctor.
treatFirst: Blood pressure that isn't yet well controlled
Heart trouble — chest pain, a recent heart attack, an irregular heartbeat, or heart failure
A thyroid that hasn't settled yet
Raised pressure in the brain, or certain neurological conditions
Seeing or hearing things others don't, or a manic episode that isn't yet being treated
notRightHeading: When this isn't the right path
notRightIntro: In these situations this work could genuinely cause harm, so it isn't offered. If that's you, it doesn't mean nothing can help — it means something else will serve you better, and Becky will point you toward it.
notRight: Schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, or psychosis that is currently active
A manic or mixed episode happening right now
Drinking or sedative use that has taken hold, or being under the influence
Pregnancy or breastfeeding, unless a doctor has specifically said it's safe
A known allergy to this medicine
A history of aneurysm, stroke, or bleeding in the brain
Thoughts of ending your life that need more immediate, intensive care than this
notRightFootnote: This isn't a complete list. Some medicines — certain mood stabilisers and anxiety medicines among them — can also change how this works. Everything is looked at properly, and individually, with the doctor overseeing your care.
closingHeading: If you're still reading, that means something
closingBody: Beginning is simpler than it looks: you reach out, and you talk. You'll say what brought you here and what you're hoping for, and together you'll work out whether this is your path. There is no pressure either way, and no commitment in asking.
